item.title: Dance Moms’ Ferocious Appetite
item.description: In the aftermath of the 2008 stock market crash, Dance Moms helped feed America's ferocious appetite for cruelty.

item.title: Craig Taborn Is at the Apex of Contemporary Jazz
item.description: In 2026, Craig Taborn and other improvisers of his generation are at the peak of their creativity. This music has rarely been more elevated, refined, and exciting.

item.title: M(h)aol’s ‘Something Soft’ Is a Post-#MeToo Gut-Punch
item.description: M(h)aol's Something Soft is a powerful feminist punk album. It highlights the stakes of inhabiting the female body in a world where safety is conditional and fleeting.

item.title: Kula Shaker Rally the Poets of Light on ‘Wormslayer’
item.description: Kula Shaker's Wormslayer is for the seeker, the adventurer, and the soul who longs for liberty—all while soundtracking their journey to an epic musical mirror.

item.title: Sammy Brue Finds Inspiration in Earle’s Journals
item.description: The Journals is a testament to the lovely friendship of Justin Townes Earle and Sammy Brue, initiated and fostered by the music they both loved.

item.title: Julian Lage Teams with John Medeski for Impeccable LP
item.description: John Medeski colors each Julian Lage composition to perfection. For all its ease of listening, this album isn't comfort food as much as a really balanced meal.

item.title: Leisure Process Deliver Treasure From the Vaults
item.description: Skittering post-disco rhythms, slap-bass riffs, synth-lines, the ebbs and flows of sax, and declamatory soaring vocals make up the sound of post-punk's Leisure Process.

item.title: Bob Weir Rides Into the Sunset for the Last Time
item.description: The Grateful Dead co-founder Bob Weir's passing away at age 78 is a significant loss for the music world, but his immense legacy will live on.

item.title: 2025 Marks Pop Music’s Gilded Age
item.description: Embracing craft alongside vulnerability in the 2020s, pop music reaches the apex of its powers in 2025 by reveling in its own glamorous facade.

item.title: 7 French Noirs for Those Long Cold Winter Nights
item.description: The French were making their own postwar brand of dark, downbeat, terse, vivid, chic, and cynical criminal melodramas before anyone ever heard the term "French Noir".
